Fixed the bug in [`_tzinfo._fromutc`](file:///work/dateutil/tz/_common.py#L204-L240) in [dateutil/tz/_common.py](file:///work/dateutil/tz/_common.py).

### Root Cause
In `_tzinfo._fromutc`, `dtdst = enfold(dt, fold=1).dst()` was previously inside the `if delta:` block (`delta = dtoff - dtdst`). For time zones with a standard UTC offset of `0` (such as `Europe/London`), `delta` is `timedelta(0)` during an ambiguous time, so `dtdst` was not recomputed with `fold=1`. As a result, `dtdst` remained `+1h` (BST) instead of `0h` (GMT), shifting `2013-10-27 01:30 UTC` to `02:30` instead of `01:30` (`fold=1`).

### Fix
Moved `dtdst = enfold(dt, fold=1).dst()` (and its `None` check) outside `if delta:` so `dtdst` is always evaluated with `fold=1` even when `delta` is zero.

### Verification
- `./venv/bin/python -m pytest -vv dateutil/test/test_tz.py -k testFoldLondon`: all 6 `testFoldLondon` tests passed (`TzLocalNixTest`, `GettzTest`, `ZoneInfoGettzTest`, `TZRangeTest`, `TZStrTest`, `TZICalTest`).
- `./venv/bin/python -m pytest dateutil/test/test_tz.py -k "not testTZSetDoesntCorrupt"`: 274 passed, 42 skipped (`TZTest::testTZSetDoesntCorrupt` fails on Python 3.13 due to an unrelated `collections.Callable` reference in `dateutil/parser.py`).
